svg.title: Daywise: conversational agent and automatic notifications
svg.desc: Messages and calendar data feed a bounded tool-using agent. A separate scheduler sends morning briefs and event check-ins. Calendar proposals require permission and fresh checks. Feedback updates the personal reward model and dashboard.

g.text: The language model chooses tools. Your personal reward model learns from ratings.
Fresh location can identify a place.
The daily brief is at 8:30 a.m.
Quiet hours and opt-outs are respected.
Events and busy intervals are live.
Observe → choose a tool → inspect the result → respond.
The model can read events, find openings, inspect learning estimates and retrieve confirmed session notes.
It runs up to four decisions per message and remembers recent turns and the exact proposal it showed you.
A follow-up such as “book it” confirms that proposal. Private dashboard codes stay outside the model.
Scheduled briefs use calendar data directly. Conflict scanning and location prompting have separate rules.
The language model is not fine-tuned. It reasons over retrieved facts and learned reward estimates.
Only real openings can be offered.
their duration and the same day.
Conflict edits check the event version.
They do not directly change scores.
Demo sessions and your own ratings
The dashboard uses a private code.
The bot must run for notifications.
Calendar availability determines possible times. LinUCB does not currently learn a time-of-day productivity effect.
